subject: Mathematics
title: Matrices and Determinants
summary: A matrix is a rectangular table of numbers (m × n). Two matrices can be multiplied only when the columns of the first equal the rows of the second, and AB is usually not equal to BA — order matters.
A determinant is a single number defined only for square matrices. It tells whether the matrix can be 'undone': |A| ≠ 0 ⇒ the inverse exists (non-singular).
The inverse comes from the adjoint: A⁻¹ = adj A / |A|. Power formulas for |adj A|, adj of adj and |kA| are JEE favourites.
Linear equations AX = B: if |A| ≠ 0 there is a unique solution X = A⁻¹B. If |A| = 0 there is either no solution or infinitely many — check with (adj A)B (or Cramer's D₁, D₂, D₃).
Determinants also give the area of a triangle and test collinearity.

formulas.name: Types of matrices
formulas.formula: Square, diagonal, scalar, identity I, zero O, upper/lower triangular, symmetric (Aᵀ = A), skew-symmetric (Aᵀ = −A, all diagonal entries 0)
formulas.note: A skew-symmetric matrix always has zero diagonal entries.

formulas.name: Special square matrices
formulas.formula: Orthogonal: AAᵀ = I.  Idempotent: A² = A.  Involutory: A² = I.  Nilpotent: Aᵏ = O (for some k)

formulas.name: Matrix multiplication
formulas.formula: (m × n)(n × p) = (m × p);   (AB)ᵢⱼ = Σₖ aᵢₖ bₖⱼ
formulas.mistake: AB = O does not mean A or B is zero; AB = AC does not give B = C.

formulas.name: Transpose rules
formulas.formula: (Aᵀ)ᵀ = A,  (A + B)ᵀ = Aᵀ + Bᵀ,  (kA)ᵀ = kAᵀ,  (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ

formulas.name: Determinant of order 2 and 3
formulas.formula: |a b; c d| = ad − bc.   3 × 3: expand along any row/column: |A| = a₁₁C₁₁ + a₁₂C₁₂ + a₁₃C₁₃
formulas.note: Expand along the row/column with the most zeros.

formulas.name: Minor and cofactor
formulas.formula: Mᵢⱼ = determinant left after deleting row i and column j;   Cᵢⱼ = (−1)^{i+j} Mᵢⱼ

formulas.name: Properties of determinants
formulas.formula: |Aᵀ| = |A|;  swapping two rows → sign changes;  two rows equal/proportional → 0;  one row × k → |A| × k;  Rᵢ → Rᵢ + kRⱼ → no change;  triangular → product of diagonal
formulas.note: Multiplying one row's entries by another row's cofactors and adding gives 0.

formulas.name: Determinant of products and scalars
formulas.formula: |AB| = |A||B|;   |kA| = kⁿ |A|  (n = order);   |Aⁿ| = |A|ⁿ;   skew-symmetric of odd order: |A| = 0
formulas.mistake: In |kA| the power of k is the order, not just k.

formulas.name: Adjoint
formulas.formula: adj A = (cofactor matrix)ᵀ;   A (adj A) = (adj A) A = |A| I

formulas.name: Adjoint properties
formulas.formula: |adj A| = |A|^{n−1};   adj(adj A) = |A|^{n−2} A;   |adj(adj A)| = |A|^{(n−1)²};   adj(AB) = (adj B)(adj A);   adj(Aᵀ) = (adj A)ᵀ

formulas.name: Area of triangle and collinearity
formulas.formula: Area = ½ |det [x₁ y₁ 1; x₂ y₂ 1; x₃ y₃ 1]|;   collinear ⇔ det = 0
formulas.when: Area from three points / whether they lie on a line.
formulas.note: Area is always positive — take the modulus.

formulas.name: System AX = B (non-homogeneous)
formulas.formula: |A| ≠ 0: unique, X = A⁻¹B.   |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O: no solution.   |A| = 0 and (adj A)B = O: infinitely many or none (check further)

formulas.name: Cramer's rule
formulas.formula: x = D₁/D, y = D₂/D, z = D₃/D  (D ≠ 0).   D = 0 with some Dᵢ ≠ 0: no solution.   D = 0 and D₁ = D₂ = D₃ = 0: infinitely many or none
formulas.note: Dᵢ = D with the i-th column replaced by B.

formulas.name: Homogeneous system AX = O
formulas.formula: Always consistent (x = y = z = 0).   Non-trivial solution ⇔ |A| = 0
formulas.when: 'Find k for a non-zero solution' questions.

formulas.name: Characteristic equation (2 × 2)
formulas.note: tr A = sum of the diagonal.

formulas.name: Trace
formulas.formula: tr(A + B) = tr A + tr B,   tr(kA) = k tr A,   tr(AB) = tr(BA)

examples.title: Determinants with powers
examples.problem: A is 3 × 3 with |A| = 4. Find |adj A|, |adj(adj A)| and |2A|.

examples.title: Area of a triangle
examples.problem: Area of the triangle with vertices (1, 2), (4, 6), (7, 2)?

examples.title: Solving three equations
examples.solution: D = |1 1 1; 1 −1 1; 2 1 −1| = 6 ≠ 0 ⇒ unique solution. By Cramer / A⁻¹B: x = 1, y = 2, z = 3. (First − second gives 2y = 4 ⇒ y = 2 at once.)

examples.title: k for infinitely many solutions
examples.problem: x + y + z = 1,  x + 2y + 3z = 2,  x + 3y + kz = 3. For which k are there infinitely many solutions?
examples.solution: D = |1 1 1; 1 2 3; 1 3 k| = k − 5. Unique for k ≠ 5. At k = 5: (eq2 − eq1) and (eq3 − eq2) both give y + 2z = 1 ⇒ consistent ⇒ infinitely many. Answer k = 5.

examples.title: Non-trivial solution
examples.problem: kx + y + z = 0,  x + ky + z = 0,  x + y + kz = 0 — when is there a non-trivial solution?

examples.title: Inverse by Cayley–Hamilton
examples.problem: A = [1 2; 3 4]. Write A⁻¹ in terms of A.
examples.solution: tr A = 5, |A| = −2 ⇒ A² − 5A − 2I = O. Multiplying by A⁻¹: A − 5I − 2A⁻¹ = O ⇒ A⁻¹ = (A − 5I)/2 = [−2 1; 3/2 −1/2].

topics.title: Order and equality of matrices
topics.explain: Order m × n = m rows, n columns. Two matrices are equal only if they have the same order and every entry matches. Addition is defined only for the same order.

topics.title: Properties of multiplication
topics.explain: Associative (AB)C = A(BC), distributive A(B + C) = AB + AC, but not commutative (AB ≠ BA in general). Identity I: AI = IA = A. Hence (A + B)² = A² + AB + BA + B², which equals A² + 2AB + B² only if AB = BA.

topics.title: Symmetric and skew-symmetric
topics.explain: AAᵀ and A + Aᵀ are always symmetric; A − Aᵀ is skew-symmetric. The product of two symmetric matrices is symmetric only if they commute. A skew-symmetric matrix has zero diagonal and, for odd order, zero determinant.

topics.title: Strategy to evaluate a determinant
topics.explain: First use properties: take out common factors, create zeros with Rᵢ → Rᵢ − Rⱼ, then expand along a row/column with zeros. If two rows look proportional the answer is 0 straight away.

topics.title: Adjoint and inverse
topics.explain: Find the cofactors and transpose = adj A. Then divide by |A|. Always check A × A⁻¹ = I. A singular matrix (|A| = 0) has no inverse.

topics.title: Consistency — complete flow
topics.explain: Step 1: find |A|. ≠ 0 ⇒ unique. Step 2: = 0 ⇒ find (adj A)B. ≠ O ⇒ inconsistent (no solution). = O ⇒ compare/eliminate the equations: if they agree, infinitely many; otherwise none.

topics.title: Homogeneous system
topics.explain: x = y = z = 0 is always a solution (trivial). If |A| = 0 there are infinitely many non-trivial ones too. 'Values of k for a non-zero solution' = solve |A| = 0.

topics.title: Geometric meaning of a determinant
topics.explain: In 2D, |det| = area of the parallelogram formed by two vectors; for three points ½|det| = area of the triangle. Area 0 ⇒ the three points are collinear.

ratta: |kA| = kⁿ|A|;  |adj A| = |A|^{n−1};  |adj adj A| = |A|^{(n−1)²};  adj adj A = |A|^{n−2} A.
A·adj A = |A| I;  A⁻¹ = adj A/|A|.
(AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ;  (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹;  adj(AB) = adj B · adj A.
D ≠ 0 unique;  D = 0 & some Dᵢ ≠ 0 → no solution.
